question: Vulnerable road users are more at risk in traffic than motorists. They are more likely to be severely injured in the event of an accident or collision. We must therefore make every effort to protect them as effectively as possible. Every year in Belgium alone, there are more than 300 accidents where a cyclist or moped rider is hit by a vehicle door opened from within the vehicle.

The ‘Dutch reach’ technique may provide a solution here. This involves opening the vehicle door using the hand furthest from the door handle. In so doing, the person opening the door automatically looks over their shoulder so that they can more easily see any approaching vulnerable road user. In the UK, it is now mandatory to use this technique. 1.
Has the Commission looked into this technique and if so, what factors were studied and what were its findings?
Is the Commission planning to include this measure in forthcoming legislation and is it also considering making it obligatory?

Are ‘physical’ measures also being considered, such as requiring manufacturers to place the door handle further back, say some 20 cm, thus automatically obliging the motorist to perform the Dutch reach?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.4.2024) The Commission takes note that on 28 February 2024, the European Parliament adopted its position in first reading on the Commission proposal to revise the Driving License Directive1. The Commission has not yet taken a position on the amendments adopted by the European Parliament, including the one that makes reference to the ‘Dutch reach’ technique.

One of the main objectives of the revision of the Driving License Directive is to enhance driver training and testing so that drivers are better prepared for the presence of vulnerable road users. This, in turn, would help improve safety for pedestrians, cyclists, as well as users of e-scooters and e-bikes, particularly in urban settings.

As such when assessing the amendments of the European Parliament, the Commission welcomes in principle amendments that further facilitate such goals, insofar as their introduction can be deemed technically feasible and proportionate. The position of door handles is not regulated, nor are handles necessarily required in vehicles (alternatives such as push-buttons exist).

In line with the ‘safety-by-design’ principle, manufacturers must design the vehicles in such a way as to permit the entry and exit in complete safety and without any danger2. The Commission has not considered further measures on the design aspects of the opening of vehicle doors.

1 COM(2023) 127 final; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52023PC0127 2 See point 2.1. in Part 2 of Annex X to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/535 laying down rules
for the application of Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 of the European Parliament and of the Council (OJ L 114, 6.4.2021, p. 1, ELI: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2021/535/oj).
